dump | | | |              1 (* TLC can read and set a special list of values while evaluating          *)
dump | | | |              2 (* expressions using the operators TLCSet and TLCGet.  When TLC evaluates  *)
dump | | | |              3 (* TLCSet(i,v), for any positive integer i and arbitrary value v, it       *)
dump | | | |              4 (* obtains the value TRUE and sets element number i of the list to v.      *)
dump | | | |              5 (* When TLC evaluates TLCGet(i), the value it obtains is the current value *)
dump | | | |              6 (* of the element number i of this list.                                   *)
dump | | | |              7 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              8 (* One use of this feature is to check TLC's progress during long          *)
dump | | | |              9 (* computations.  For example, suppose TLC is evaluating a formula         *)
dump | | | |              10 (* \\A x \\in S : P where S is a large set, so it evaluates P many times.    *)
dump | | | |              11 (* You can use TLCGet, TLCSet, and Print to print something after every    *)
dump | | | |              12 (* 1000 times TLC evaluates P.                                             *)
dump | | | |              13 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              14 (* As explained in the description of the TLCEval operator below, you may  *)
dump | | | |              15 (* also want to use this feature to count how many times TLC is evaluating *)
dump | | | |              16 (* an expression e.  To use value number i as the counter, just replace e  *)
dump | | | |              17 (* by                                                                      *)
dump | | | |              18 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              19 (*   IF TLCSet(i, TLCGet(i)+1) THEN e ELSE 42                              *)
dump | | | |              20 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              21 (* (The ELSE expression is never evaluated.)                               *)
dump | | | |              22 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              23 (* TLCGet accepts some pre-defined string values to query TLC state. The   *)
dump | | | |              24 (* values are as follows:                                                  *)
dump | | | |              25 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              26 (*   - TLCGet("distinct") evaluates to the total number of distinct states *)
dump | | | |              27 (*     found by TLC so far, globally.                                      *)
dump | | | |              28 (*   - TLCGet("queue") evaluates to the number of states currently in the  *)

dump | | | |              33 (*     found by TLC so far, globally (equals one in the initial predicate).*)
dump | | | |              34 (*   - TLCGet("level") is the length of the current behavior (equals zero  *)
dump | | | |              35 (*     in the evaluation of the initial predicate).                        *)
dump | | | |              36 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              37 (* For reasons of efficiency, TLCGet and TLCSet behave somewhat strangely  *)
dump | | | |              38 (* when TLC is run with multiple worker threads.  Each worker thread       *)
dump | | | |              39 (* maintains its own individual copy of the list of values on which it     *)
dump | | | |              40 (* evaluates TLCGet and TLCSet.  The worker threads are activated only     *)
dump | | | |              41 (* after the computation and invariance checking of the initial states.    *)
dump | | | |              42 (* Before then, evaluating TLCSet(i,v) sets the element i of the list      *)
dump | | | |              43 (* maintained by all threads.  Thus, the lists of all the worker threads   *)
dump | | | |              44 (* can be initialized by putting the appropriate TLCSet expression in an   *)
dump | | | |              45 (* ASSUME expression or in the initial predicate.                          *)
dump | | | |              46 (*                                                                         *)

dump | | | |              7 (*                                                                         *)

dump | | | |              1 (* TLC can read and set a special list of values while evaluating          *)
dump | | | |              2 (* expressions using the operators TLCSet and TLCGet.  When TLC evaluates  *)
dump | | | |              3 (* TLCSet(i,v), for any positive integer i and arbitrary value v, it       *)
dump | | | |              4 (* obtains the value TRUE and sets element number i of the list to v.      *)
dump | | | |              5 (* When TLC evaluates TLCGet(i), the value it obtains is the current value *)
dump | | | |              6 (* of the element number i of this list.                                   *)
dump | | | |              7 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              8 (* One use of this feature is to check TLC's progress during long          *)
dump | | | |              9 (* computations.  For example, suppose TLC is evaluating a formula         *)
dump | | | |              10 (* \\A x \\in S : P where S is a large set, so it evaluates P many times.    *)
dump | | | |              11 (* You can use TLCGet, TLCSet, and Print to print something after every    *)
dump | | | |              12 (* 1000 times TLC evaluates P.                                             *)
dump | | | |              13 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              14 (* As explained in the description of the TLCEval operator below, you may  *)
dump | | | |              15 (* also want to use this feature to count how many times TLC is evaluating *)
dump | | | |              16 (* an expression e.  To use value number i as the counter, just replace e  *)
dump | | | |              17 (* by                                                                      *)
dump | | | |              18 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              19 (*   IF TLCSet(i, TLCGet(i)+1) THEN e ELSE 42                              *)
dump | | | |              20 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              21 (* (The ELSE expression is never evaluated.)                               *)
dump | | | |              22 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              23 (* TLCGet accepts some pre-defined string values to query TLC state. The   *)
dump | | | |              24 (* values are as follows:                                                  *)
dump | | | |              25 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              26 (*   - TLCGet("distinct") evaluates to the total number of distinct states *)
dump | | | |              27 (*     found by TLC so far, globally.                                      *)
dump | | | |              28 (*   - TLCGet("queue") evaluates to the number of states currently in the  *)

dump | | | |              33 (*     found by TLC so far, globally (equals one in the initial predicate).*)
dump | | | |              34 (*   - TLCGet("level") is the length of the current behavior (equals zero  *)
dump | | | |              35 (*     in the evaluation of the initial predicate).                        *)
dump | | | |              36 (*                                                                         *)
dump | | | |              37 (* For reasons of efficiency, TLCGet and TLCSet behave somewhat strangely  *)
dump | | | |              38 (* when TLC is run with multiple worker threads.  Each worker thread       *)
dump | | | |              39 (* maintains its own individual copy of the list of values on which it     *)
dump | | | |              40 (* evaluates TLCGet and TLCSet.  The worker threads are activated only     *)
dump | | | |              41 (* after the computation and invariance checking of the initial states.    *)
dump | | | |              42 (* Before then, evaluating TLCSet(i,v) sets the element i of the list      *)
dump | | | |              43 (* maintained by all threads.  Thus, the lists of all the worker threads   *)
dump | | | |              44 (* can be initialized by putting the appropriate TLCSet expression in an   *)
dump | | | |              45 (* ASSUME expression or in the initial predicate.                          *)
dump | | | |              46 (*                                                                         *)
